lines.japanese: 日和子さんが洗面所で顔を洗っている間、俺はひとり、これからのことについて考えていました。
lines.english: While Hiyoko washed her face in the washroom, I stayed behind alone and thought about what came next.

lines.japanese: いままで逃げていたこと。目を逸らしていたこと。考えないふりを続けていたこと。そう、それは俺の──
lines.english: What I had spent all this time running from. What I had refused to look at. What I had gone on pretending not to think about. Yes: my—

lines.japanese: ──俺たちの、特殊な事情のこと。現状、俺の体は俺だけのものじゃないこと。
lines.english: —our unusual circumstances. The fact that, as things stood, my body was not mine alone.

lines.japanese: 本気で恋愛を始めるなら避けては通れない問題です。カミングアウトしないわけにも行かないでしょう。
lines.english: If I meant to begin a real relationship, there was no avoiding it. Sooner or later, I would have to come out with the truth.

lines.japanese: 「あの、お待たせしました」
lines.english: “Um, sorry to keep you waiting.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、おかえりなさい。えーと、じゃあ俺このフロア、掃除しておきますんで。日和子さんは、続けて着替えてきちゃってください」
lines.english: “Oh, welcome back. Right, then—I'll clean up down here. You go on and get changed.”

lines.japanese: 「鷲介さんだけにやらせてしまってすみません。お願いします」
lines.english: “I'm sorry to leave it all to you, Shusuke. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、その前にちょっといいすか」
lines.english: “Oh—before you go, can I ask you something?”

lines.japanese: 「はい？」
lines.english: “Yes?”

lines.japanese: 俺が呼びとめたとき、日和子さんは上の更衣室へ向かおうと、階段に足をかけたところでした。
lines.english: When I stopped her, Hiyoko had just put one foot on the stairs to the changing room above.

lines.japanese: 「なんでしょう」
lines.english: “What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「えーとー」
lines.english: “Well...”

lines.japanese: さて、どう切りだしたもんでしょう。俺は前髪に息を当てながら考えてみました。
lines.english: Now, how was I supposed to broach it? I blew at my bangs while I considered the problem.

lines.japanese: 「まだマスターにも言ってないことなんですけどー」
lines.english: “I haven't even told the boss this yet...”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 「俺、日和子さんに話しておきたいことがあるんですよ」
lines.english: “There's something I want to tell you, Hiyoko.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 「ていうか、すいません訂正します。話しておかなきゃならないことです。話したら日和子さん離れていっちゃうかもしれないけど、でも話さないわけにはいかないことなんです」
lines.english: “Actually, sorry. Let me correct myself. It's something I have to tell you. You may want nothing more to do with me afterward—but I can't keep it from you.”

lines.japanese: 「それで、あの……ふたりで落ちついて話せるところがいいんですけど、日和子さん、明日ってバイトの前に時間とれませんか？」
lines.english: “So, um... I'd like somewhere quiet, where the two of us can talk. Do you have any time before work tomorrow?”

lines.japanese: 「いまでも構いませんよ」
lines.english: “We could talk now.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、ちょっと時間がかかりそうなんで……これ以上日和子さんの帰りを遅らせるわけにもいかないですし」
lines.english: “No, it may take a while... and I can't keep you any later tonight.”

lines.japanese: 「そうですか。じゃあ明日ですね、分かりました」
lines.english: “I see. Tomorrow, then. I understand.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとうございます。えと、あの、あんまり面白い話じゃないんですけど……いいっすか？」
lines.english: “Thank you. Um, it isn't exactly a fun story... Is that okay?”

lines.japanese: 「昨日は鷲介さんに話を聞いてもらいましたから、今度は私の番です」
lines.english: “You listened to me yesterday, Shusuke. Now it is my turn.”

lines.japanese: 「大切な話なんですよね」
lines.english: “It is important, isn't it?”

lines.japanese: あからさまに面倒な話という雰囲気を漂わせているのに、日和子さんはいつも通りの表情であっさり了解してくれました。こんな優しいひとを好きになれてよかったと思います。
lines.english: I could hardly have made it sound more like a troublesome conversation, yet Hiyoko accepted with her usual composure. I was glad I had fallen in love with someone so kind.

lines.japanese: もし日和子さんが、俺たちの事情を聞いて受けいれられなかったとしても、きっと後悔しないでいられるような気がしました。
lines.english: Even if she heard the truth about us and could not accept it, I felt certain I would never regret having loved her.

lines.japanese: 「それじゃあ明日バイト前、何時でもいいんで、俺の家に来てください」
lines.english: “Then come to my place before work tomorrow. Any time is fine.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ！」
lines.english: “What!?”

lines.japanese: 俺の家、という単語に日和子さんは過剰反応なさいました。
lines.english: Hiyoko reacted rather strongly to the words “my place.”

lines.japanese: 「や、あの、べつにやましい連れ込み根性とかじゃないですからね？　単に、誰にも聞かれたくない話ができる場所を選んだだけですからね？」
lines.english: “N-no, listen, this isn't some dirty-minded scheme to get you alone at my place, okay? I only chose somewhere we could talk without anyone overhearing us.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そんなことは分かってます。じゃあ、鷲介さんの家に行けばいいんですよね」
lines.english: “I-I know that. So I just need to go to your house, right?”

lines.japanese: 「お願いします。あ、うちの住所は……」
lines.english: “Please. Oh, my address is...”

lines.japanese: 羽田邸への道筋をざっくり説明し、二階へあがる日和子さんを見送ったあと、俺はひとりフロアの清掃に入りました。
lines.english: I gave her the rough directions to the Haneda house, watched her go upstairs, and began cleaning the floor by myself.
“Whew...”

lines.japanese: クローズ作業を一通り終えて柔軟体操。
lines.english: Once I had run through the closing routine, I did a few stretches.

lines.japanese: ふと時計を見ました。開始約２０分。シングルスのタイムとしてはまあ上等ですよね。工藤さん、俺やったよ！
lines.english: I glanced at the clock. About twenty minutes from the starting gun. A respectable time for the singles event, wouldn't you say? Kudo, I did it!

lines.japanese: えーっと、日和子さんは……まだ戻ってこないな。着替えってそんなに時間かかるのかな。もしかして、疲れて眠っちゃったとか？　だったら可哀想だけど起こしてあげなきゃな。
lines.english: Now, Hiyoko was... still not back. Did changing really take that long? Maybe she'd fallen asleep from exhaustion. Poor thing—but if she had, I would have to wake her.

lines.japanese: うん、とにかく掃除も終わったことだし、俺も事務室へ上が──
lines.english: Well, the cleaning was done, so I might as well go up to the office myse—

lines.japanese: ──ん？　あれ？　これは、誰かが外階段を下る音？
lines.english: —Hm? What? Was that the sound of someone going down the outside stairs?

lines.japanese: 誰かって、そりゃ日和子さんしかいないよな。えー、先に帰っちゃったのか。たしかに、一緒に帰る約束なんてしてなかったけどさ、ちぇー。
lines.english: And ‘someone’ could only have been Hiyoko. What, had she gone home without me? True, we had never promised to leave together, but still. Hmph.

lines.japanese: 少し残念に思いつつ、それでも事務室へは向かいました。戸締りのため、お店の鍵を取りに行かねばなりません。
lines.english: Disappointed though I was, I went to the office anyway. I had to fetch the shop keys so I could lock up.

lines.japanese: あれ？
lines.english: Huh?

lines.japanese: 事務室に入ると明かりが点いたままになっていました。あ、そうか俺のためにか。ああんもう、日和子さんったら気の利く子なんだから。
lines.english: The office light was still on when I entered. Oh, of course—she had left it on for me. Oh, Hiyoko, you thoughtful little thing.

lines.japanese: さらに目的の鍵束が、分かりやすーく机の真ん中に置かれています。ああんもう、日和子さんったらどこまでも優しい子なのかしら。もう惚れてしまいそうですわ。
lines.english: And there, where no one could possibly miss them, sat the keys I had come for, right in the middle of the desk. Oh, Hiyoko, could you be any sweeter? Why, at this rate I shall fall in love with you.

lines.japanese: どころか、すでにＺｏｋｋｏｎだけどな！
lines.english: As if I weren't already completely head over heels!

lines.japanese: さ、帰るか。
lines.english: Right. Time to go home.
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 鍵を拾うために近付くと、その下に一枚の紙きれが敷いてありました。手帳から切りはなしたのでしょうか、縦長変型の罫線入りです。
lines.english: When I came closer to pick up the keys, I found a slip of paper underneath them. Torn from a planner, perhaps: long and narrow, with ruled lines.

lines.japanese: 手に取ってみると、さながら隼人君のように筆圧の強い、たどたどしくもダイナミックな文字（一瞬、小学生向けの暗号絵文字かとも思いました）が、びっしりと並んでいます。
lines.english: I picked it up. The page was packed with halting yet dynamic letters, pressed into the paper with the same force Hayato used. For a moment I took them for a picture cipher intended for grade-school children.

lines.japanese: な、なんだろう、このある種ほほえましささえ覚えるブサイク文字の羅列は。マスターの覚え書きか何かか？
lines.english: Wh-what was this procession of ugly little symbols—so ugly, in its way, that it was almost charming? Some note the boss had jotted down?

lines.japanese: 古代の呪いでも発動しそうな奇怪きわまる紙面でしたが、もしマスターの残していった俺宛てのメモだとしたら、無視するわけにも参りません。意を決して、俺は目を通すことにしました。
lines.english: The page looked capable of awakening an ancient curse. Still, if the boss had left me a note, I could hardly ignore it. I steeled myself and began to decipher.

lines.japanese: 『鷺大ち人∧』
lines.english: ‘To Heron-Big-chi-Person-Caret’

lines.japanese: む、いきなり難解だな……なんて読むんだコレ。「鷺」ってなんだ、ええとサギって読むんだっけ？　知るか、こんな漢字。まあ、一瞬だけなら鷲介の「鷲」に見えないことも──
lines.english: Hm. Cryptic from the very first line... How did you even read this? Was that first character “heron”? Who knew a character like that? Although, if you only glanced at it, it did look a little like the first character in Shusuke—

lines.japanese: ──あ、あれ？　コレもしかして鷺じゃなくて鷲か？　あっ、そうみたいだ。ああ、なるほど「鷲介さんへ」って書いてあるのか。
lines.english: —W-wait. Maybe it wasn't “heron” at all, but the first character in Shusuke? Ah! Yes, apparently so. I see. It says, “To Shusuke.”

lines.japanese: てことは？　ん？　千歳鷲介をそう呼ぶのは世界でただひとりのはず。あッ！　ままままさか、ここここのグロテスク暗号の書き置きは、軽部店長じゃなくて──
lines.english: Which meant...? Hm? There was only one person in the world who called Shusuke Chitose by that name. Ah! D-d-don't tell me this grotesque cipher hadn't been left by Manager Karube at all, but by—

lines.japanese: <8>\　日和子さん！？
lines.english: Hiyoko!?

lines.japanese: うぞおおおーんっ、何このド下手くそ……もとい、個性あふれる前衛的な文字！
lines.english: No waaaay! What was this catastrophically terrible... I mean, magnificently individual and avant-garde handwriting!?

lines.japanese: はっ！　そういえばあの子、前に言ってたな。前担当さんに「アナログ原稿だと選考で不利になるかも」って言われたと……。
lines.english: Wait! Come to think of it, she had told me once. Her old editor said, “Submitting a handwritten manuscript may put you at a disadvantage in the judging”...

lines.japanese: な、なるほど、こういう意味だったのか。たしかに頷ける話だ。前担当さん、日和子さんを傷付けないための婉曲表現ありがとう。
lines.english: I-I see. So that was what he meant. Certainly made sense now. Thank you, former editor, for finding a euphemism that spared Hiyoko's feelings.

lines.japanese: ま、まあいいや、日和子さんの書いた手紙だと思えば、うん、急に可愛らしい乙女文字に見えてきたぞ（鷲介ちょっぴり無理してます）。
lines.english: W-well, never mind. Once I remembered it was a letter written by Hiyoko, yes, it suddenly looked like the adorable hand of a young maiden. (Shusuke is forcing it a little.)

lines.japanese: 『クローズを鷲介さんだけに任せてしまいすみません』
lines.english: “I am sorry for leaving all the closing work to you, Shusuke.”

lines.japanese: よし、怪異的な印象から構えて見ちゃったけど、冷静に見れば実はそこまでひどくもないな。うん、読める読める。たぶん。
lines.english: Good. Its eldritch appearance had put me on guard, but looked at calmly, it was not really that awful. Yes, I could read it. Probably.

lines.japanese: 『使った道具類はきちんと洗って、元の場所に戻しておいてください。冬なので水洗いが大変だとは思いますが、いい加減に済ませて早番のひとに迷惑をかけたりはしないように』
lines.english: “Please wash every utensil you used properly and return it to its place. I know washing in cold water is difficult in winter, but do not do a halfhearted job and leave trouble for the opening shift.”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい、すいません」
lines.english: “Y-yes, ma'am. Sorry.”

lines.japanese: まるで鬼教官の声が聞こえてくるようで、思わずただの紙きれに頭を下げてしまいました。
lines.english: I could practically hear my demonic drill instructor's voice, and found myself bowing to a mere scrap of paper.

lines.japanese: 『戸締りの方法ですが、鍵と一緒に青い棒があるので、それを入り口脇の機械に差しこんでください』
lines.english: “As for locking up: beside the keys is a blue rod. Insert it into the machine by the entrance.”

lines.japanese: 『棒を引きぬくとブサーが３０秒鳴るので、必ずその間に鍵をかけること。３０秒経過するとセキュリティー会社に緊急連絡がいってしまうので、先にしっかり位置を確認してから戸締りをしてください』
lines.english: “When you pull out the rod, the buzer will sound for thirty seconds. You must lock the door before that time is up. After thirty seconds an emergency report will be sent to the security company, so make absolutely sure you know where everything is before locking up.”

lines.japanese: ふーん。ただのバタン、ガチャじゃないのか。なんか微妙にめんどくさいんだな。
lines.english: Huh. So it wasn't just slam, click, and done. What a pain.

lines.japanese: や、でも日和子さん、こんな長々と書いてくれるんだったら、俺に直接口頭で説明してくれた方が早かっただろうに。
lines.english: Still, Hiyoko, if you were going to write all this out, surely it would have been quicker to explain it to me in person.

lines.japanese: あ……ひょっとして、俺と帰るのが嫌だったのか？　一時は情に流されてあんなことしちゃったけど、冷静になってみたら後悔が押しよせてきて、やがてそれは激しい嫌悪感へと……！？
lines.english: Ah... Could it be that she hadn't wanted to walk home with me? Maybe emotion had swept her into doing all that, but then she had calmed down, regret had come flooding in, and before long it had curdled into violent disgust...!?

lines.japanese: いやいや、そんなことはない……と思うけど……でもなあ、結局んとこ俺が一方的に告白して、交際申しこんで、なし崩しにあんなことまでしちゃったけど、いまだ彼女からの明確な返事はもらってないんだよなあ。
lines.english: No, no. That couldn't be it... I didn't think... But then, when you came right down to it, I had confessed to her, asked her out, and somehow blundered straight into all that without ever receiving a clear answer from her.
“Sigh...”

lines.japanese: ソファーに倒れこんで溜息こぼしながら、だるだるテンションで残りの作業指示を確認しました。
lines.english: I collapsed onto the sofa and sighed, then read the remaining instructions with all the spirit of a wet dishrag.

lines.japanese: 『シャッターはＢの刻印がある鍵です。こちらは普通に施錠していただければ大丈夫ですが、安全に関わることなのでくれぐれもミスのないようお願いします』
lines.english: “The shutter takes the key stamped B. You may lock this one normally, but it is a matter of security, so please take every possible care not to make a mistake.”

lines.japanese: へいへい、っと。
lines.english: Yeah, yeah. Got it.

lines.japanese: 『鍵は明日、鷲介さんから店長に返しておいてください。これも一方的に棚へ戻すことは厳禁です。小さな伝達ミスもしばしば大きな損害へ繋がります。必ず一声かけるように』
lines.english: “Tomorrow, please return the keys to the manager in person. It is strictly forbidden to put them back on the shelf without telling him. Small failures of communication often lead to large losses. Make certain you speak to him.”

lines.japanese: へーいへい、っと。
lines.english: Yeees, yes. Got it.

lines.japanese: 『追伸　今日は本当にごめんなさい。次はがんばります。機会があれば恋人にしてください』
lines.english: “P.S. I am truly sorry about today. Next time I will do better. If you will have me, please let me be your girlfriend.”

lines.japanese: へいへい分かりましたっての。まーったくこの鬼教官は、相変わらずひとつも可愛げの──
lines.english: Yeah, yeah, I understand. Honestly, this demonic drill instructor was as completely devoid of charm as ev—

lines.japanese: ──ええええッ！　うそおおーん、可愛げめちゃめちゃあるじゃないですかァァァー！？
lines.english: —WHAAAAAT!? No waaaay! She's got charm coming out of her eeeeeears!

lines.japanese: 『追伸　今日は本当にごめんなさい。次はがんばります。機会があれば恋人にしてください』
lines.english: “P.S. I am truly sorry about today. Next time I will do better. If you will have me, please let me be your girlfriend.”

lines.japanese: 思わず二度見してしまいましたが、目の錯覚ではありませんでした。
lines.english: I read it again at once, but my eyes had not deceived me.

lines.japanese: 「あわ、あわわわわ……」
lines.english: “Awa—awawawawawa...”

lines.japanese: あまりの衝撃に縮みあがってしまった俺は、いつものようにきゃっほう！　と飛びあがることすら失念していました。
lines.english: The shock shriveled me so completely that I even forgot to spring into the air with my customary yahoo!

lines.japanese: 「ひ、ひひひ日和子さんが……あの日和子さんが、かかか可愛いこと言ってる……」
lines.english: “H-H-H-Hiyoko... Hiyoko of all people just said s-s-something adorable...”

lines.japanese: がちがち震えながらメモを裏返すと、紙面の隅っこに小さく「しゅうすけ／ひよこ」の相合傘が描かれてありました。
lines.english: Trembling violently, I turned the note over. In one corner, very small, she had drawn a lovers' umbrella with ‘Shusuke’ and ‘Hiyoko’ beneath it.

lines.japanese: 「ひぃぃぃ──ッ！？」
lines.english: “Eeeeeeeeeeeek!?”

lines.japanese: 未曾有の衝撃は恐怖にさえ似ていて、パニックを引きおこした俺は、思わずソファーの上で身悶えしながら形而上の尿をびしゃびしゃ撒きちらしておりました。
lines.english: The unprecedented shock was almost terror. In my panic, I writhed across the sofa, spraying metaphysical urine everywhere.

lines.japanese: 「し、死ぬ……俺、キュン死にする……」
lines.english: “I-I’m dying... She’s so cute I’m going to die...”

lines.japanese: 説教くさい文面も、おどろおどろしい文字も、不揃いすぎて「ひょこ」としか読めない相合傘も、すべてが愛しくてたまりません。しばらく俺は、彼女の残したメモ紙に頬を擦りよせるのでした。
lines.english: The preachy prose, the ghastly handwriting, even the lovers' umbrella so misshapen that ‘Hiyoko’ looked like ‘Hyoko’—I adored every last bit of it. For some time, I rubbed my cheek against the note she had left behind.

lines.japanese: 日ょ子さんの指示通りに各階の戸締りをして、あとはシャッターさえ下ろせば全行程終了……というところで、俺は車道の真ん中まで下がってみました。
lines.english: I locked each floor according to Hyoko's instructions. With only the shutter left before the entire procedure was complete, I backed out into the middle of the road.

lines.japanese: 見上げる建物はレンガ作りで三角の屋根。そして頭に伸びている煙突。どこか滑稽にも見えるこの店において、俺が最後に出るのは意外とこれが初めてでした。
lines.english: I looked up at the brick building: its triangular roof, the chimney rising from its crown. There was something comical about the shop, yet, surprisingly, this was the first time I had ever been the last one out.

lines.japanese: 「楽しいなあ」
lines.english: “This is fun.”

lines.japanese: いまの俺の偽らざる心境です。
lines.english: That was exactly how I felt.

lines.japanese: 隼人君。鷹志君。会わなかったみんな。ありがとう。
lines.english: Hayato. Takashi. All the others I never had the chance to meet. Thank you.

lines.japanese: おやすみアレキサンダー。
lines.english: Good night, Alexander.

lines.japanese: また明日。
lines.english: See you tomorrow.
